taxonomyNote: Formerly placed in the genus Eleutherodactylus (NatureServe); NatureServe notes subspecies latrans and cactorum have been proposed as separate species but it currently recognizes no subspecies.
fieldMarks: Toad-shaped frog 64.5-75 mm with a large head and small truncated toe pads.
Greenish to tan, smooth skin with scattered dark spots; dorsolateral skin folds on the back, one fold across the back of the head, and a disk-shaped fold on the belly.
Young are often greenish with a fawn band across the middle of the back.
behavior: Nocturnal; call carries like a dog's bark at a distance and sounds like a throaty 'whurr' close up.
Breeds with rain: February-May in Texas, late June-July in Arizona; eggs are laid on land under rocks, logs or in crevices and there is no free-living tadpole stage.
Walks with the body held high and inflates to several times normal size when threatened; most active at night during rains.
habitat: Low-elevation rocky shrubland, desert and woodland, often on limestone or rhyolite outcrops, in caves or crevices or rodent burrows; under rocks or logs, including oak and juniper woodland in Texas.
range: Central Texas to southeastern New Mexico and south into Mexico; NatureServe lists Arizona, New Mexico and Texas. Not recorded for Canada.
